case_name: Ananda Poojary v State of Karnataka
respondent:
State of Karnataka
Supreme Court of India

14 October 2014
Cr.A. No. 2202 of 2014 (Arising Out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 7185 of 2013)
The Judgment was delivered by : Arjan Kumar Sikri, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. By this appeal, the appellant Ananda Poojary questions the legality and validity of the judgment dated 14.02.2013 passed by the High Court of Karnataka, whereby the appellant's conviction for offences u/s. 302 and S. 201 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') has been upheld. The High Court has also upheld the sentence passed by the Sessions Judge, Udupi. The result is that the appellant is made to suffer incarceration for life for allegedly murdering his own foster mother.
3. It is an admitted position, accepted by the two courts below, that the deceased Dorathi Kutinho, who was a Teacher, had brought Ananda Poojary (the appellant) who was her student to her house and had showered love and affection like a mother. In her old age, there was nobody to look afte
facts: The High Court has upheld the conviction of Ananda Poojary for murdering his foster mother Dorathi Kutinho.
Dorathi Kutinho had executed a Will bequeathing all her movable and immovable properties to Ananda Poojary, but with one condition: he must marry a Christian lady.
Ananda Poojary was found guilty of murder by the Sessions Court and the High Court.
The case against Ananda Poojary was based on circumstantial evidence, as there were no eyewitnesses to the crime.
The prosecution relied on evidence from various witnesses, including PW-1 to PW-14, Exs.P-1 to P-46, and Mos.1 to 5.
issues: Whether the courts below are right in their conclusion that Ananda Poojary had become the destroyer of Dorathi Kutinho's life.
Whether the motive for murder was established by the prosecution.
Whether the evidence presented by the prosecution is sufficient to prove Ananda Poojary's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
petitioner_arguments: The appellant denied the incriminating evidence found in the evidence of the prosecution against him.
The defence maintains that Dorathi Kutinho died natural death due to cardiac arrest, not murder.
There was no other person except the appellant, deceased and Rudolph who were residing in the house of the deceased.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution relied on evidence from various witnesses, including PW-1 to PW-14, Exs.P-1 to P-46, and Mos.1 to 5.
The motive for murder was established by the recovery of articles and deposition of PW-3.

The various ingredients proved by the prosecution are sufficient to complete the chain of circumstances to come to a definite and unerring conclusion that the appellant must be the person who had committed the murder.
court_reasoning: The trial court held it to be a case of murder after analysing the testimony of various witnesses.

The sessions court has rested its findings by taking into consideration the following circumstances: execution of Will, recovery of articles, deposition of PW-3, and other evidence presented by the prosecution.
holding: The Supreme Court upholds the conviction of Ananda Poojary for murdering his foster mother Dorathi Kutinho.
The case is remanded to the High Court for further consideration in light of new evidence.
